_why: Every post in this batch targets a miss-you keyword, and /missyou-gf is the template built for exactly that reader, so it is genuinely mandatory rather than an opt-out. The verifier's built-in default (mandatory /bouquet-gf) is the bouquet-wave policy and would force an off-topic digital-bouquet link into a post about saying 'I miss you' in Tagalog. oneOfLinks is the batch's give-another-option rule: each post must also name one genuine ALTERNATIVE with the reason it suits that reader better — /train-ticket or /streak for long distance, /catch or /photo-puzzle when the sender wants a letter rather than a page, /hold-my-hand for the reader who cannot say it in words, /capsule when the missing is about time rather than distance, /dedication when a song says it better, /apology-dashboard when the missing follows a fight, /love-gf when the message is really 'I love you'. The 2-4 internal links from TEMPLATE_LINKS rule still applies and is enforced separately.
_capExemptWhy: These are reference INSTRUMENTS, not publishers with a point of view. Six posts checking six different languages against the same dictionary or the same Unicode chart is method, not publisher concentration — the cap exists to stop nine posts leaning on one press release. The verifier counts body links, so without this exemption the batch's own language-verification requirement would fail it. Every one of these still has to be fetched and still has to say what the post claims it says. EXTENDED 2026-09-25: national dictionaries, state language portals and lexical databases (RAE, Treccani, CNRTL, Académie, DWDS, Priberam, STDict, Gramota, the Russian National Corpus, KWF's diksiyonaryo.ph, Cologne's Sanskrit lexicon, Perseus, Jisho, WALS, ASL-LEX, ISLRTC, SIL's webonary) are reference instruments by the same argument as the dictionaries already listed. Six posts citing six DIFFERENT national dictionaries is method; the rule exists to stop nine posts leaning on one press release. This was added after diksiyonaryo.ph hit the cap and closed the Philippine national dictionary to the batch's later Philippine posts, which is the rule working against its own purpose. EXTENDED AGAIN 2026-09-25, and this one is a rule-design correction rather than a convenience: PMC, Europe PMC, PubMed, Google Books, archive.org and Project Gutenberg are REPOSITORIES, not publishers. Three papers reached through PMC are typically three different journals, which is the opposite of the concentration the cap exists to prevent. Counting the host cost this batch two real sources: the i-miss-you-in-arabic agent lost a paper on Arabic diglossia AND orthographic complexity (its exact subject), and the i-miss-you-in-russian agent lost Hentschel 2023 on Ukrainian-Russian Suržyk after reading it in full. Both recorded re-check triggers. THE CAP STILL APPLIES, but to the JOURNAL or publisher named in the citation, not to the repository host: no journal in more than 3 posts, and agents must name the journal so this is checkable by hand. EXTENDED 2026-09-26 for the multilingual batch: every national dictionary, usage authority and corpus named in BRIEF.md section 4 is a reference INSTRUMENT, not research concentration. A post that verifies a Turkish line against TDK and a Polish line against PWN is showing its method; capping those would push agents to cite a competitor listicle instead, which is the exact failure the cap exists to prevent. EXTENDED 2026-09-27: e-ans.ivdnt.org (the ANS) reached 3/3 while BRIEF section 4 names it as THE Dutch authority - a reference grammar is an instrument, not research concentration, and capping it would push rows to cite a listicle instead. Same reasoning for grammis (IDS), lessicografia (Crusca), DIEC2/DCVB, the Real Academia Galega, TDK, and the OQLF.
capExemptNote: 2026-09-28: only en.wiktionary.org was exempt, in a batch covering 15+ languages — so a German or Polish row hit the domain cap on the obvious dictionary while the English row did not. Wiktionary is one instrument per language edition and the exemption rationale (a dictionary has exactly one correct citation) applies identically, so every language edition in scope is now listed. Wikisource is deliberately NOT exempt: it hosts primary literary texts, which are not in the enumerated instrument classes. Also 2026-09-28: NKJP (pelcra-nkjp.clarin-pl.eu), Wortschatz Leipzig, DWDS and sjp.pwn.pl added — all corpora or dictionaries, i.e. already covered by the stated rationale, and all were being capped. dictionary.reverso.net is deliberately NOT added: Reverso is a commercial aggregator, not an authority, so the cap on it is correct. 2026-09-28 (wave 5): dem.colmex.mx added — the Diccionario del español de México (El Colegio de México) is an authoritative dictionary and was counting against the domain cap while dle.rae.es was exempt, which in a ten-row Spanish batch penalises the best mx-es instrument. Same rationale as every other dictionary here. 2026-09-28 (wave 5, second fix): capcheck PRINTS "statutes, dictionaries, treebanks, corpora and standards are EXEMPT" but exempts by HOSTNAME, and the list carried unicode.org while omitting every other standards body. Result: UAX #15 was exempt while RFC 3986 and the Open Graph spec were flagged banned in the same post. Added rfc-editor.org, ietf.org, datatracker.ietf.org, w3.org, ogp.me, iso.org, whatwg.org — a standards document has exactly one correct citation, which is the whole rationale.
